headline: Angel One Limited: Disclosure under SEBI Takeover Regulations
sum: Dinesh Thakkar filed a substantial acquisition disclosure under SEBI Regulation 31(4), signalling a material shareholding or stake change in Angel One Limited with the NSE.
implication: Regulation 31(4) disclosure is mandatory when an acquirer crosses the 25% threshold or undertakes a creeping acquisition; this filing triggers potential open-offer obligations under Regulation 38 if the threshold is exceeded, requiring Thakkar to publicly disclose acquisition intent and offer terms.
detail: The disclosure was filed with the NSE under the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011. Dinesh Thakkar submitted the Regulation 31(4) form, which is required when a person or group acquires shares exceeding prescribed thresholds. The exact quantum of shares acquired and the consideration are not disclosed in the headline document excerpt but would be contained in the full filing on the NSE archive.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, Regulation 31(4)
framework.note: Mandatory disclosure requirement for acquirers crossing 25% or engaging in substantial share acquisition; triggers open-offer regime if threshold exceeded.
Open offer obligation triggered if substantial acquisition threshold is crossed; acquirer must make binding offer at fixed price to public shareholders.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992, Section 15(2)
framework.note: SEBI's authority to frame regulations governing substantial acquisitions and takeovers to protect investor interests.

framework.ref: Companies Act, 2013, Section 149(1) and Schedule IV
framework.note: Director and board composition rules; may apply if Thakkar's acquisition qualifies as control change requiring board reconstitution.

framework.ref: Listing Agreement / SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
framework.note: Angel One's obligation to disseminate the disclosure to stock exchanges and shareholders in real time.
If Thakkar is an insider or related party, acquisition may be subject to trading windows and disclosure restrictions.
